question: What is the boxed warning on Eliquis?

route.reason: A boxed warning is part of the FDA drug label for apixaban (Eliquis), so this question is answered by the label source only.

draft.text: Eliquis (apixaban) carries a boxed warning with two parts. (A) Premature discontinuation increases the risk of thrombotic events: stopping any oral anticoagulant, including Eliquis, raises this risk [label:apixaban:boxed_warning:0]. If Eliquis is stopped for a reason other than pathological bleeding or completion of a course of therapy, consider coverage with another anticoagulant [label:apixaban:boxed_warning:0]. (B) Spinal/epidural hematoma: epidural or spinal hematomas may occur in patients receiving neuraxial anesthesia or undergoing spinal puncture, and these may result in long-term or permanent paralysis [label:apixaban:boxed_warning:0]. Consider these risks when scheduling patients for spinal procedures [label:apixaban:boxed_warning:0]. Factors that can increase the risk include indwelling epidural catheters, concomitant drugs affecting hemostasis (such as NSAIDs, platelet inhibitors, other anticoagulants), a history of traumatic or repeated epidural or spinal punctures, and a history of spinal deformity or spinal surgery [label:apixaban:boxed_warning:1]. The optimal timing between Eliquis administration and neuraxial procedures is not known [label:apixaban:boxed_warning:1]. Patients should be monitored frequently for signs and symptoms of neurological impairment, and urgent treatment is necessary if neurological compromise is noted [label:apixaban:boxed_warning:1].
